messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency was a significant independent predictor of depression in CKD patients, with higher odds of depression among those deficient.
Sentence: "Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that vitamin D deficiency was a significant independent predictor of depression after adjusting for confounding factors (adjusted odds ratio, 6.15; 95% confidence interval, 2.02-8.75; P = 0.001)."
Measured as: depression (WHO CIDI-Short Form)
Population: 533 patients with chronic kidney disease from KNHANES V, VI (2010-2014), mean age 70.1 years
Intervention: Vitamin D deficiency (serum 25(OH)D3 ≤10 ng/mL), observational exposure
Comparator: Vitamin D sufficient CKD patients
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 533
baseline_vitamin_d_status: at_or_above_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: Vitamin D level was significantly related to risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5) six months after COVID-19 hospital admission; the direction is not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "The variables that were significantly related to the risk of depression 6 months after admission for COVID-19 were frailty (p = 0.006 for pre-frail and p = 0.001 for frail), small-vessel vascular disease in imaging tests (p = 0.033), vitamin D level (p = 0.006), and taking antidepressants (p = 0.011)."
Measured as: risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5)
Population: 72 patients admitted to a hospital in Spain for COVID-19, assessed at discharge and six months later
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both findings concern vitamin D exposure and depression, but Study A is cross-sectional in CKD patients with a deficiency-depression association, while Study B is a cohort of COVID-19 survivors with a direction not stated, so the results point different ways across populations and designs.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["design_or_bias"],"detail":"population: CKD patients vs COVID-19 hospital survivors; design: cross-sectional vs cohort, direction unstated in Study B"}
